body.x: [Las Vegas, U.S. = Aving News] “At this moment, the vision and entrepreneurship that will be the new driving force for Seoul 15 years from now, or even further in the future, are being conceived. Seoul Business Agency is arguably the best accelerator in the public sector for speeding up the growth.”

At Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S. on the 6th (local time), Hyun Woo Kim, CEO of the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), expressed his sense of responsibility and pride in their task of helping create and develop Korean startups.

At CES 2023, SBA operated the Seoul Tech Pavilion, which introduced Seoul’s future vision and innovative technologies, and the K-Startup Joint Pavilion, which demonstrated technologies of 51 businesses, showcasing innovation by a total of 66 businesses. In particular, 14 of the participating companies won in the CES 2023 Innovation Awards.

Seoul Tech Pavilion, taking up an area about 165 ㎡ in size, was set up in the North Hall of the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC), which is the main exhibition hall of CES. Under the theme of “Seoul: Smart Transportation and Eco-friendly City,” the Pavilion implemented the future vision of Seoul with the innovative technology of outstanding Korean businesses, providing various attractions for visitors with 3D videos on giant screens, technology demonstrations from cooperating businesses, and a metaverse experience booth. Exhibition participants’ open pitches on their technology, Smart City Seoul Forum, and investment attraction events were also held.

In Eureka Park at the Venetian Expo, the 473 ㎡ sized K-Startup Joint Pavilion showcased excellent technologies of 51 businesses located in Seoul. Organizations such as the Seoul Business Agency, Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, and Seoul Business Agency worked together to run this event.

The exhibition spaces were divided into five areas: ▲mobility, ▲bio and healthcare, ▲ESG (Environment, Social, Governance), ▲manufacturing, and ▲data. Various field programs such as Global Demo Day, Startup Talk Show, and a networking event called Meet the K-Startup were also held.

Such diverse programs and the exhibition strategies prepared and implemented for Korean startups attending CES 2023 were backed by extraordinary vision and drive of the Seoul Business Agency’s CEO Hyun Woo Kim.
On the 6th (local time) at CES 2023, Aving News was able to have an insightful conversation with SBA’s CEO Kim, who has been leading the preparations for this exhibition.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: I know that you have a very busy schedule during this CES.

A. CEO Kim: Today is the second day of the event. Yesterday, which was Day 1, was quite hectic. We successfully ran the “Vision Declaration Ceremony” held at the Seoul Joint Pavilion. I'd like thank all of the visitors for attending the event.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: So, what's your impression of the event so far?

A. CEO Kim: I felt that the atmosphere in Eureka Park at the Venetian Expo where the K-Startup Joint Pavilion is located is quite different from that in the LVCC exhibition hall, the main exhibition hall at CES 2023. With “young” businesses gathered together, the K-Startup Joint Pavilion seemed more active and lively.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: You are in charge of everything that the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) handles. Could you tell us a bit about the SBA?

A. CEO Kim: To put it simply, I think you can say that the agency is the best “accelerator” in the public sector. SBA spares no effort to provide all possible support for the growth of all SMEs and startups in Seoul, help them make leaps in advancement.

For example, we provide research and development funds or procure marketing policies and expenses to help them pave their entry into domestic and foreign markets, and sometimes we act as an investor for different activities for their businesses. Furthermore, we support various efforts by, for example, attracting investment from overseas investment institutions.

body.x: Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Many startups and smart-city related businesses based in Seoul participated at CES 2023. What are your thoughts about this?

A. CEO Kim: First of all, the K-Startup Pavilion presents companies that have been rigorously evaluated by the host, CTA, for their vision, technology, and competitiveness. It is a very promising result that 51 of them are participating.

Moreover, the Seoul Tech Pavilion in LVCC North Hall is the first case in CES history of a city’s joint pavilion being set up in the hall. I think Seoul’s charm has played a role here. With “Smart Mobility,” among various lifestyles featured in Seoul, as the theme, we participated in Open Innovation and offered a variety of products and technologies by our companies which were well-received by the audience.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: It's a bit early to talk about the outcomes, but are there any noteworthy achievements that you can share?

A. CEO Kim: I’ve heard that participating companies are actively arranging and having business meetings in the exhibition. Among them, INFINIQ, known for its satellite technology, is in talks for two new contracts. LiBEST is also demonstrating their technology and has received a positive response. I am happy to see that we are getting what we were hoping for before the start of CES 2023.

Large-scale enterprises simply can’t possess all of the technology they need. That’s why they seek partnership with startups. By hosting Open Innovation, SBA facilitates such processes by supporting startups. LiBEST is one of the beneficiaries and is an exemplary case.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: The global industry is still suffering from the longstanding war and pandemics, so how is that affected CES 2023?

A. CEO Kim: CES is also influenced by specific global issues and conflicts. In previous years, Chinese visitors could be found anywhere in the exhibition hall, but the recent conflict between the United States and China has prevented Chinese businesses from entering the U.S. market. So, the number of Chinese participants in CES 2023 has dropped dramatically.

You can also see, depending on each country's industry and system status, Japan sent fewer participants, while French and South Korean attendees increased. I think this is an indicator pointing at the main drivers behind the global industry in the future. This year’s CES will matter more than ever for startups in Korea, and we hope they will take advantage of the opportunity.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: I believe you must feel a heavy responsibility in achieving the expected results as CEO. How do you feel about that?

A. CEO Kim: I am doing my best as always, but for this year’s CES, I have put even more effort. That's because I think that something that will drive Seoul in the next 15 years, or even longer than that, is being conceived at this point in time. For those great ideas to become reality, I know how important our agency’s role is in identifying industry trends and nurturing businesses based on the insights we gain here.

body.cap: Hyun Woo Kim, CEO of the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S. on the 6th (local time) | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: How are the trends identified by the SBA in CES 2023 going to be applied to future business supporting policies?

A. I haven't had a chance to look around the entire exhibition hall. However, from what I've seen and heard so far, the global market including the U.S. is focusing on and expanding the smart mobility and healthcare sectors. I was able to see a number of businesses with advanced technology in those fields, and their booths were quite popular among visitors.

We plan to make sure that the insights gained by businesses and institutions are actively shared. By sharing opinions and information through panel discussions, for example, we will help those who weren’t able to participate in the event to understand, even indirectly, the atmosphere and future trends found in CES.

In addition, we are considering ways to support business officials who don’t have their own booths to explore and experience the site in person. This could also be another way for them to enhance the competitiveness of their business.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Among other domestic companies, there is a significant number of businesses in Seoul getting the spotlight in CES 2023. Is there anything you would like to say to them?

A. CEO Kim: I believe everyone is feeling that the way the world thinks about South Korea and Seoul is very different from the way it used to be. There are so many Koreans roaming around CES 2023 that I even feel like the event is taking place in Korea, which mirrors the new status of the country.

Watching corporate officials from Seoul enjoying this atmosphere, actively networking and gaining different insights, made me feel very proud. If you come up with any ideas on how we can better conduct our efforts, please feel free to suggest your opinions. We will do our best to put your great ideas to use.

Meanwhile, CES, the world's largest IT fair, is an exhibition that provides a comprehensive look of the global consumer electronics industry in just one place. It is held annually in Las Vegas in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). Aving News has annually reported on CES news for the world for 17 consecutive years since 2006, hosting the Best of CES which selects the best innovative products and technologies, and the Best of Made in Korea that chooses the most innovative businesses in South Korea. In addition, the media has delivered breaking news about CES through AVING LIVE.
